title: I Used 5 Password Managers for a Month. One Is Clearly Better.
creator: Sam Whitfield
description:
A month, five password managers, one very confused family. I tested autofill, sharing, recovery, and how annoying each one is on a phone.

Not sponsored. No affiliate links. I paid for every plan I tested.

0:00 Intro
0:35 Disclaimer
1:05 Setup and import
2:10 Autofill
3:05 Family sharing
3:50 Recovery test
4:30 My pick

sentences.t: Last month I moved my whole family between five different password managers, one week each, and they almost disowned me.
I wanted to know which one actually works for normal people, not just for nerds like me.
So, my parents, my partner, and my fourteen year old, who has opinions about everything.
Before anything else, I need to say something, because it matters for a video like this.
Two of the companies in this video, 1Password and Bitwarden, have sponsored videos on this channel in the past.
This video is not sponsored by anyone, not by them and not by anyone else.
None of these companies knew I was making it, nobody saw it before you did, and I paid for every plan myself.
There are no affiliate links in the description, so I make exactly nothing if you pick one of them.
Okay, with that out of the way, the five were 1Password, Bitwarden, Proton Pass, Dashlane, and KeePassXC.
First test, importing, because if moving your passwords in is painful, nobody's going to do it.
My dad had four hundred passwords saved in Chrome, some of them from two thousand and nine.
Everything except KeePassXC pulled them in from a CSV file in a couple of minutes.
KeePassXC did it too, but it took me twenty minutes on the phone with my dad, explaining what a file is.
Second test, autofill, and this is where the differences really show up.
1Password was the smoothest on the iPhone, like, it just knew what I wanted almost every time.
Bitwarden was close, but on Android it kept offering my partner's bank login on my kid's game account, which was alarming.
Dashlane was fine on desktop and weirdly slow on mobile, there was this half second pause every single time.
Proton Pass surprised me, it was quick and clean, and it made those hide-my-email aliases right inside the signup form.
Third test, family sharing, and this is the one I really care about.
I wanted my parents to see the streaming logins and the wifi password, and absolutely nothing else of mine.
1Password and Bitwarden both do shared vaults really well, you drag an item in and it's just shared.
Dashlane's sharing worked, but my mum couldn't find the shared items in the app, and honestly neither could I.
KeePassXC basically doesn't do this, you'd be passing a database file around, and that's a no from my family.
Last test, and the scary one, recovery.
I had my partner pretend she forgot her master password and lost her phone on the same day.
With 1Password, the family organizer, that's me, could recover her account in about five minutes.
With Bitwarden we'd set up emergency access, and that worked too, but there's a waiting period you have to sit through.
Proton Pass had a recovery phrase she'd written down, which worked, because she actually wrote it down.
If she hadn't, she would have been locked out, which is the honest trade-off with these things.
So, my pick for a normal family, at the end of all this.
If money isn't tight, the one my whole family liked best was 1Password, by a mile.
If you want free, or close to free, Bitwarden is still excellent, it's just a little rougher around the edges.
And if you're privacy obsessed and patient, Proton Pass is the one I'd keep an eye on.
My kid's verdict, by the way, was that they're all annoying and he'd rather just remember everything, which, good luck.
Tell me in the comments what your family uses, and thanks for watching.
